item.text:
**Verdict:** Mixed, leaning negative. I found some real 2024 evidence of technocratic insulation in macro policy and procurement, but the stronger pattern is that Erdoğan’s state kept using regulatory, judicial, property, and media levers in politically aligned ways. I did not find a clean 2024 case where a named Erdoğan family or business interest clearly won a public contract or license; the closest direct family-interest evidence is allegation-based.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Turkey central bank chief quits, citing need to protect her family | Reuters | 2024-02-02 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/turkey-central-bank-chief-resigns-after-aggressive-rate-hikes-3291652 | Erdoğan replaced the departing CBRT governor with technocrat Fatih Karahan and the tightening program continued. That is weak but real evidence of allowing a professional policy team to keep operating rather than turning the bank into a personal/family instrument, though the same report notes Erdoğan had already fired the prior four governors. | 7B.3; 6B.9 |
| Positive | Turkey’s top court rules to annul key parts of last year’s decree law | Hürriyet Daily News / Reuters | 2024-06-05 | https://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/top-court-rules-to-annul-key-parts-of-last-years-decree-law-197090 | The Constitutional Court struck down provisions that had let the president dismiss central-bank governors before term end. That is direct evidence of institutional constraint on personal control over a core state decision channel. | 7B.3; 6B.9 |
| Positive | DMO foreword on transparency and digital procurement | Devlet Malzeme Ofisi Genel Müdürlüğü | 2024-05-03 | https://www.dmo.gov.tr/Eng/Home/EngIcerik/1212 | The state procurement agency says its system emphasizes transparency, competition, accountability, and digital e-tenders. This is concrete evidence that at least one public-contract lane was being run through formal rules rather than obvious patronage. | 7B.3; 5B.6; 6B.9 |
| Positive | DMO Health Market expansion and savings | Devlet Malzeme Ofisi Genel Müdürlüğü | 2024-10-17 | https://www.dmo.gov.tr/Home/Icerik/3992 | DMO says centralized, digital procurement covered most hospital drug and medical-supply demand and generated savings. That supports a rule-based, professional procurement channel rather than a family- or clique-run one. | 7B.3; 5B.6 |
| Negative | Turkey’s CB governor faces accusation of family influence on bank operations | Turkish Minute | 2024-01-18 | https://www.turkishminute.com/2024/01/18/turkeys-cb-governor-faces-accusation-of-family-influence-on-bank-operations/ | A formal complaint alleged the governor’s father influenced operations, personnel, and use of facilities at the central bank. This is not adjudicated proof, but it is directly relevant evidence that family influence was believed to be intruding into a state institution. | 7B.3 |
| Negative | Shock and confusion as Turkey seizes earthquake survivors’ homes | Reuters | 2024-03-18 | https://www.reuters.com/commodities/shock-and-confusion-as-turkey-seizes-earthquake-survivors-homes-2024-03-18/ | Reuters reported thousands of Hatay property deeds transferred to the Treasury under an urban-planning amendment, with broad discretionary authority and unclear compensation. That is a strong example of state property power being exercised in a politically fraught, non-neutral way. | 7B.3 |
| Negative | Türkiye: Government Removes Elected Opposition Mayors | Human Rights Watch | 2024-11-07 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/11/07/turkiye-government-removes-elected-opposition-mayors | HRW says elected mayors were removed, councils dissolved, and trustees appointed using terrorism allegations after opposition wins. That is direct evidence that law enforcement and local administration were used to neutralize political rivals rather than kept separate from ruling-party interests. | 7B.3; 7B.2 |
| Negative | Turkey | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey | The report describes tight media control, RTÜK fines on critical outlets, and disproportionate airtime for incumbents. This shows the information environment was managed to protect ruling interests, not kept cleanly separate from political power. | 7B.3; 7B.2 |

Search gap: I did not find a high-confidence 2024 Reuters/AP item showing Erdoğan personally directing a family business to win a named public contract or license. The best direct family-interest material was allegation-based around the central bank governor’s family; the strongest overall evidence is indirect, through capture of procurement, property, media, and local-government power.
